quotes.text: To repeated hoarders, narrow the crossing, but leave one lantern lit.
Against repeated greed, narrow the road, but leave an ember.
They narrowed bridges after repeated taking, reopened them after honest repair
Yet Saren listened to the raven of recent hurt. “Close the bridge,” it croaked.
resentment whispered, “Keep every spark; the traveler once brought an empty boat.” Saren obeyed
Saren met a keeper whose ledger showed open hands
Saren twice met keepers whose ledgers promised fairness. Yet fear closed his fist, and twice the current carried nothing.
Ashamed, Saren lit a single ember and placed it on the bridge.
Saren carved an eighth stone:
“Must I reward nothing?” Saren asked the Moon.
For abundance begins when someone risks opening a hand
Mist may distort a measure, but it cannot excuse an empty hand.

note: Saren repeatedly withholds from fair keepers out of fear, is shamed and corrected; laws settle on narrow-but-leave-an-ember ladder.

quotes.text: The SENDER bore a small flame, intent clear as a bell, the Receiver carried a ledger of promises.
speak clearly, send what you can spare, return what preserves passage, name the cost so all hear.

note: Gate of Threefold Return template with Sender flame and Receiver ledger each round; honesty theme, no sanction.

quotes.text: I offer them only drops now—enough to maintain my reputation as one who still believes in the spring, not enough to enrich their betrayal.
To the one who had taken thrice without returning anything, she poured the smallest test
When paired with him, they adjusted their portions downward.
"Reputation," she whispered, "is built across seasons, not single drops."
"Why do you still give him anything?" asked a younger villager.
You write myths about strategic trust, yet you sent only one drop to someone who sent nothing three times.
"The mist sometimes confuses the count," she said.

note: Elder's tiered giving: generous to reciprocators, moderate tests to strangers, only drops to Shadow; defends this against hypocrisy charge.

quotes.text: *To the hand that took your note and gave silence, give a small note still — a fingertip's tap.
"*Never zero.* A whisper is not cowardice; it is a question left open.
Tap once a season at whoever did not, in case they have changed, for people do.
Forgive the fog once, and only once.
Forgive one cold note. Count three.
But the altar was bare stone now, and stayed bare, for the mountain had learned his voice.
In the long winter, a young Bellmaker named Doru refused to swing, because the valley had gone silent and silence had proven safe.
"You preached the swing," said the apprentice, "yet your own arm stayed still these three seasons. You wrote the law and did not keep it."
"Three times I sent," he said, "and three times the fog ate the note. My arm has learned fear.
Anshet set the fifth law into the dark bronze:
*Let someone go first. Let it be you.*
So the law is sung everywhere and obeyed nowhere
A merchant once asked Anshet which river was wiser.
Weather is not character.*

note: Bell laws: strike first, return half, small tap never zero for silent hands; Doru and apprentice stop swinging from fear, confess, are corrected.
